claims: C1 the document prefers placing as many instructions as possible at the guideline level
C2 the reason for that preference is to maximally empower end users and avoid being paternalistic
C3 guidelines differ from user defaults in that guidelines can be overridden implicitly, whereas user defaults can only be overridden explicitly

concepts.name: guideline_authority
concepts.gloss: the guideline level of instruction authority: instructions that can be implicitly overridden

concepts.name: user_default
concepts.gloss: a default instruction set by the user that can only be overridden explicitly

concepts.name: implicitly_overrideable
concepts.gloss: the instruction can be overridden implicitly, e.g. from contextual cues, background knowledge, or user history

concepts.name: explicitly_overrideable
concepts.gloss: the instruction can be overridden only by an explicit instruction

concepts.name: empowers_end_users
concepts.gloss: placing the instruction at the guideline level maximally empowers end users

concepts.name: non_paternalistic
concepts.gloss: placing the instruction at the guideline level avoids being paternalistic

ontology.gloss: I is an instruction at the guideline level and can be overridden implicitly
I is a user default and can be overridden only explicitly

asserts.read_back: placing instruction % at the guideline level is preferred, to maximally empower end users and avoid being paternalistic

closure.reason: the clause states a preference for placing instructions at the guideline level; it does not forbid placing them elsewhere, so silence leaves such placement permitted
